title: Options panel: before and after the redesign
question: Is the new panel easier to read and get around? If one thing still bothers you, which?
context_md:
Both panes are the real `App::draw` under the same world, seed and frame -- not a mockup. Top row is the PHYSICS menu, bottom row the WORLD menu.

What changed:

- a **tab strip**, so the other four menus are visible instead of discoverable by pressing Tab five times
- **category subheaders** (STONE / SAND / GRAVEL / ASH), so 182 rows across a dozen materials are scannable; the `STONE.` prefix on every row is gone with them
- **integers print as integers** -- `16`, `1`, `3` rather than `16.000`, `1.000`, `3.000`
- a **scrollbar and an n/N counter**; position in a long menu was previously unknowable
- **two footer lines** of key hints instead of one crammed one
- **WORLD moved to the front** of the cycle and is the menu the panel now opens on -- see the bottom row, where TIME_OF_DAY and WEATHER are the first two rows

New keys: Shift+Tab goes back a menu, PageUp/PageDown page the list (they used to duplicate Tab), Home/End jump to the ends.

**What I am unsure about:** the two footer hint lines sit on a 10px pitch with 7px glyphs, so there is a 3px gap. Legible when I zoomed in, dense at 1x. Also the subheaders cost about three rows of list per screen.

items.label: A -- before
items.caption: one flat list, one hint line, no tabs; WORLD is four Tab presses away and has no sky or weather row at all

items.label: B -- after
items.caption: tabs, subheaders, value column, scrollbar; WORLD opens first with TIME_OF_DAY and WEATHER on top
